title: Inductive Bias Alignment: Which Architectures Have Safety-Favorable Inductive Biases?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: The connection between architecture inductive biases and alignment is theoretically motivated but the causal chain is long. Even if one architecture scores better on proxy measures, translating this to deployment-relevant safety recommendations requires many additional steps.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training three different architectures on the same task is feasible. Measuring activation linearity and monosemanticity is moderately technical. Sensitivity to spurious correlations requires designing appropriate test sets. Overall achievable with mentor support.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three architectures, three different proxy metrics, plus theoretical comparison. Each architecture-metric combination is a mini-experiment. The total work easily exceeds 30 hours even with simple setups.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
